subject: Derivative guardrails / Order Form redlines — DataForge
messages:
From: Claire Rivers <claire.rivers@dataforge.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Holt <ben.holt@dataforge.com>, legal@dataforge.com
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DF order form redline: output ownership, training, feedback license

Marcus —

Attached are DataForge's redlines to the MSA + Order Form (see DataForge_Redlines_20261125.docx). High level asks:
- DataForge wants assignment/clear ownership of any productized output that is unique to our data.
- No model training using customer data unless explicitly agreed; telemetry for quality improvements is OK if anonymized.
- We want a broad feedback license so DataForge can use feedback we provide across our product line.

Can Redwood confirm how you typically handle: output title vs. productization rights; a carveout for customer-specific training; scope/term of a feedback license? We need this answered before procurement signs off. Ben and I are on a tight Q4 schedule.

Thanks,
Claire Rivers
Senior Counsel — DataForge Inc.
Attachments: DataForge_Redlines_20261125.docx (docx)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Claire Rivers <claire.rivers@dataforge.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 25 Nov 2026 11:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DF order form redline: output ownership, training, feedback license

Claire —

Thanks for sending this over and for the clear summary. We're aligned on the urgency. I'll loop in Legal (Laura) and our CS lead (Sean) to propose workable language quickly. A couple quick notes so we're explicit:
- Redwood's standard approach is to allow customers to own "productized output" (what the Order Form calls "Customer Output"). Where customers need assignment for downstream commercialization we can support that, but we typically exclude training the service on customer-specific data without an opt-in.
- Telemetry: we can permit anonymized/aggregated telemetry for quality and safety improvements; need to agree retention limits.
- Feedback license: we usually accept a limited, non-exclusive license for Redwood to use customer-provided feedback to improve the service, but we can draft a reciprocal clause for DataForge to use its own feedback internally.

Laura — can you propose precise redline language for: (1) an output/productization assignment pathway that preserves our ability to serve other customers; (2) a clause that prevents model training on DataForge content unless DataForge signs the training opt-in (order form addition); and (3) a feedback license that splits rights clearly?

Claire / Ben — I'll follow up with a short playbook and a proposed Order Form edit by EOD tomorrow.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference — marcus_lin@redwood.com

From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Claire Rivers <claire.rivers@dataforge.com>, sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 26 Nov 2026 08:45:00 -08:00
Subject: RE: DF order form redline: output ownership, training, feedback license

Marcus / Claire —

Attached is a short summary plus precise redline suggestions (summary-derivative-language-20261126.txt). Below are the recommended edits with rationale. I kept language tight to preserve Redwood's runtime/product freedom while giving DataForge the commercial certainty they need.

1) Customer Output / Productization pathway (Order Form - Section 3):
Proposed: "Customer shall retain ownership of Customer Output where Customer has supplied the input data. To the extent Customer requires assignment of any developed deliverable for downstream commercialization, the Parties may execute a separate Assignment Addendum on commercially reasonable terms. Redwood retains the right to use de-identified or generalized outputs for service improvement not tied to Customer's Confidential Data."
Rationale: Allows assignment by addendum (gives procurement a path) but prevents blanket assignment that would limit our model/feature reuse.

2) Training / Model Use (MSA - Data Use section):
Proposed: "Redwood will not train, fine-tune, or adapt customer-specific models using Customer Content unless Customer affirmatively opts into the Training Addendum on the Order Form. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Redwood may process anonymized and aggregated telemetry for quality and safety improvements; such telemetry will not include Customer PII and will be retained for no longer than 180 days unless otherwise agreed."
Rationale: Strong opt-in for training; clear telemetry guardrails and retention window.

3) Feedback License (MSA - Feedback clause):
Proposed: "Customer grants Redwood a perpetual, worldwide, non-exclusive, royalty-free license to use Customer Feedback to operate, improve, and commercialize the Service, provided that such use does not disclose Customer Confidential Information or identifiable Customer Output. Redwood grants Customer a limited, non-exclusive license to use its own Feedback for its internal productization purposes."
Rationale: Keeps feedback useful to us, but prevents disclosure of CI; grants customer internal rights for their own feedback.

Open item: DataForge's initial redline asked for assignment without an addendum — we should push back and offer the Assignment Addendum path above.

Next steps I suggest: Marcus send this redline back to Claire with an explicit ask for the procurement/finance contact to sign the Assignment Addendum when/if needed. Sean, can you confirm with CS/ops that the 180-day telemetry retention is operationally feasible?

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: summary-derivative-language-20261126.txt

From: Claire Rivers <claire.rivers@dataforge.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Holt <ben.holt@dataforge.com>, legal@dataforge.com
Date: Fri, 27 Nov 2026 10:00:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: DF order form redline: output ownership, training, feedback license

Laura / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear redline language. The Assignment Addendum approach is acceptable to DataForge provided the addendum includes a 3-year carveout for the specific products we plan to commercialize (we'll propose specifics in the addendum).

A couple clarifying points:
- The telemetry retention window of 180 days is fine. Please include a clause that Redwood will provide a quarterly report of telemetry types collected (high-level categories only).
- Feedback license: we need to confirm that "Customer Feedback" does not include outputs that we expressly assign under an Assignment Addendum.

If you can incorporate the two clarifications, I think we can move to final redlines and routing to procurement next week.

Regards,
Claire Rivers
Senior Counsel — DataForge Inc.
